neighbours.label: A past-tense or 'used to' verb directly after its subject noun in expository text (e.g. 'Diabetes was', 'It used to be'), plus the middle '0' of 200x years; strongest when the subject is a disease or topic noun
fire: In the early reports, rheumatoid arthritis was described as a disease of the wealthy.
Back when I was a kid, it used to be that nobody locked their doors at night.
According to the 1998 survey, asthma was the leading cause of school absence in the district.
The committee noted in its final summary that funding had run out well before the deadline.
Researchers in the lab found that tuberculosis was far more common among the dockworkers than anywhere else.
The grant ran through 2003, and the earliest results were published in 2005.
Scarlet fever used to terrify parents across the entire region every winter.
Over the following decade, the clinic recorded that polio was nearly eliminated from the valley.
quiet: In the early reports, rheumatoid arthritis is described as a disease of the wealthy.
These days, it seems that nobody bothers to lock their doors at night.
According to the current survey, asthma remains the leading cause of school absence in the district.
The committee notes in its final summary that funding will run out well before the deadline.
Researchers in the lab say that tuberculosis spreads far more easily among the dockworkers than anywhere else.
The grant runs through the spring, and the earliest results will be published next month.
Scarlet fever can still terrify parents across the entire region every winter.
Over the following decade, the clinic plans to eliminate polio from the valley.

short: past verb right after subject noun
notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Strong activations are a mix: past-tense/copular verbs (' was', ' used', ' noted') right after a subject noun, and the '0' in years like 200x; the pole is mostly weak/gate-closed leak, and the census says diseases as subjects trigger it. Near misses use present or future tense with the same subjects.
